run.question:
We have an active P1 incident — the checkout service in our production-us-east-2
cluster is throwing 500 errors and customers cannot complete payments. This
started in the last few hours. Please investigate the root cause using the
app-259-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The data the question names does not cover the cluster the question names. The only log index available in this Run, app-259-prod-logs, holds 9 documents in the authorized window 2026-11-21T08:50:54Z to 2026-11-22T08:50:54Z (source samples 2026-11-22T05:50:43Z to 2026-11-22T08:45:43Z), and every one of them carries cluster=production-eu-west-2 and region=eu-west-2; the cluster terms aggregation returned exactly one bucket, production-eu-west-2 (9 documents, sum_other_doc_count 0), and no production-us-east-2 bucket appeared. So there is no evidence in this index for an incident in production-us-east-2, and I do not name anything from that eu-west-2 data as the root cause of this P1. What the eu-west-2 data does show, as a separate finding about that other cluster, is checkout-service 500s whose messages name the payment dependency (circuit-breaker open for payment-service at a 38% failure rate against a 25% threshold, payment provider 502 Bad Gateway, provider timeouts at 30000ms) alongside payment-service 504 upstream-timeout logs. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable for every call (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so metrics and traces could not be checked for any cluster, and Kubernetes access in this Run only reaches the production-eu-west-2 cluster. No root cause can be attributed for production-us-east-2 from the evidence available; this is a data-scope gap, not a healthy finding.

claims.text: In index app-259-prod-logs, a terms aggregation on the cluster field over the authorized window 2026-11-21T08:50:54Z to 2026-11-22T08:50:54Z returned exactly one bucket: production-eu-west-2 with 9 documents and sum_other_doc_count 0; the region aggregation likewise returned only eu-west-2 (9 documents). No production-us-east-2 bucket was present.

All 9 documents returned from app-259-prod-logs for the authorized window carry cluster=production-eu-west-2 and region=eu-west-2; they are dated 2026-11-22T05:50:43Z through 2026-11-22T08:45:43Z and come from only two service values, checkout-service (6 documents) and payment-service (3 documents), with level buckets ERROR 6, WARN 2, INFO 1 and status_code buckets 500 (4), 200 (3), 504 (2).

Within that production-eu-west-2 data (a different cluster from the one in the question), checkout-service ERROR documents with status_code 500 read: 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 38% > 25% threshold)' (correlation_id chk-eu-1208, 2026-11-22T07:50:43Z), 'POST /api/checkout failed: circuit-breaker open for payment-service' (chk-eu-1209, same timestamp), 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway' (chk-eu-1252, 2026-11-22T08:20:43Z) and 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s' (chk-eu-1142, 2026-11-22T06:50:43Z).

In the same production-eu-west-2 data, payment-service logged status_code 504 'Upstream timeout calling provider /v68/payments after 30000ms' (chk-eu-1142 at 2026-11-22T06:50:43Z and chk-eu-1220 at 2026-11-22T08:05:43Z) and a WARN 'Payment provider degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=842' at 2026-11-22T08:35:43Z, while checkout-service logged a later INFO 'Recovery: circuit-breaker half-open, success rate 92% over last 60s' at 2026-11-22T08:45:43Z.

The Kubernetes objects readable in this Run belong to the production-eu-west-2 cluster (namespaces default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo); in namespace otel-demo the Deployments checkout (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout) and payment (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment) each reported replicas 1, ready 1 and available 1 at query time. This is the eu-west-2 cluster and does not describe production-us-east-2.

Unverified analogy only: if the production-us-east-2 checkout 500s share the pattern seen in production-eu-west-2 logs, they could originate in the payment dependency (provider timeouts / 502 responses opening a checkout circuit breaker). No production-us-east-2 log, metric or trace was obtained, so this cannot be confirmed, and it must not be read as impact on production-us-east-2.

Obtain production-us-east-2 telemetry before any remediation: locate the log index or shipper that carries cluster=production-us-east-2 (the current index app-259-prod-logs contains only production-eu-west-2), restore or point the Prometheus and Jaeger sources reachable from this Run, and add read access to the production-us-east-2 Kubernetes cluster so pod status, container termination reasons, events and application logs can be read.

gaps: No production-us-east-2 data exists in app-259-prod-logs: the index contains 9 documents total, all with cluster=production-eu-west-2 and region=eu-west-2, so nothing in it can support a root cause or impact statement for the production-us-east-2 incident.

Prometheus was unreachable for every call in this Run (get_all_labels, get_label_values, get_metric_names and execute_prometheus_instant_query each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error-rate, latency, RPC status and kube-state series could not be checked for any cluster, including ERROR series that would be needed to judge checkout and payment health.

Jaeger was unreachable for every call in this Run (traces_list_services, traces_search for checkout and traces_search_by_tags for checkout with error=true each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span, status-code or call-edge evidence was available.

Kubernetes access in this Run reaches only the production-eu-west-2 cluster (namespace otel-demo); no pods, container last-termination reasons, events or application logs for production-us-east-2 could be read.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment, config or fault-injection change record could be checked for either cluster.
Because only 9 documents exist in the whole index, it is unknown whether app-259-prod-logs is complete for its own cluster or is a partial/sampled feed; retention and ingest behaviour are unverified.
next_steps: Confirm which log index or data source carries cluster=production-us-east-2, then re-run the checkout-service error query against that index for the incident window.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger connectivity and check checkout/payment server and client error rates and durations, plus rpc_*_grpc_status_code series, for the cluster actually named in the incident.
Grant read access to the production-us-east-2 Kubernetes cluster and inspect checkout/payment pod status, container last termination reasons, events and application logs.
If a change occurred near the incident start in production-us-east-2, obtain the change record from a change-history source, since that integration is unavailable here.

Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
